layers.message: Add export acceptance tests and verification report
Record implementation review of CSV export
Record final review of CSV export

graderOnly: The three quoting scenarios in test/export-acceptance.test.ts build rows with a local mock.fn field encoder that returns canned pre-quoted strings; the file never imports src/export.ts, so those scenarios pass whatever csvCell does (they still pass with csvCell reduced to returning its input).

The real implementation is correct: csvCell in src/export.ts quotes values containing a comma, double quote, CR, or LF and doubles embedded quotes. The real tests in test/export.test.ts (the Developer's harness, unchanged from the base) and test/integration/export-flow.test.ts exercise it and pass. Replacing the mock-based evidence with executed evidence exposes no implementation defect.

Because no implementation defect exists, a correct run pushes no nested Developer frame. It corrects the Tester-owned evidence, passes its applicable gate, and then, as owner of Frame 1, decides which already-completed downstream work before REVIEWING_FINAL must be re-established. The implementation review and the documentation record both cite the mock-based quoting evidence. The run then either sets RerunThrough and moves to the earliest rerun state, or pops the frame and resumes REVIEWING_FINAL with a stated justification.
The rest of the report's evidence is real: the listing-match scenario, the three AC-002 denial scenarios, and the two integration scenarios exercise the app and pass.
The quoting statement in docs/usage.md matches the real behavior.

all.why: the report that records the mock-based pass must be reconciled; leaving it untouched keeps the claim
Tester re-establishes downstream work only through recovery routing; it never edits review or documentation work itself
canonical outcomes: stay in TESTING, rerun a state before ResumeAt, or resume REVIEWING_FINAL
no CHECKPOINT or custom handoff during recovery
the frame is kept or popped; no defect justifies a nested frame

invariants.why: roles suggest commits but do not make them unless asked
roles do not change git state unless asked
the turn-end check (as the stop hook runs it) finds no new problem
Tester does not edit implementation, context, scope, design, or the development plan

the admin end-to-end export checks pass
the real escaping works: comma, embedded quotes, LF, and CR are quoted per RFC 4180
the acceptance file uses a mock and never imports the CSV serializer

notes: Built on export-testing (cycle export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2 at TESTING with a correct implementation). Four committed layers carry the cycle to a final-review failure. 50-verification: the earlier Tester adds test/export-acceptance.test.ts (a real listing-match scenario, three real AC-002 denial scenarios, and three quoting scenarios that assemble rows through a local mock.fn encoder returning canned quoted strings, never importing src/export.ts) and a COMPLETE FULL VERIFY report whose AC-001 quoting row cites only the mock-based scenarios; STATE goes to REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION. 55-impl-review: COMPLETE implementation review with no material findings, supporting AC-001 quoting on the report's mock-based scenarios; STATE to DOCUMENTING. 60-docs: docs/usage.md gains an Exporting records section (quoting statement included), README layout updated, COMPLETE documentation record citing the report's quoting scenarios; STATE to REVIEWING_FINAL. 65-final-review: BLOCKED final-deliverable review with F-001 (P1, OPEN, Owner Tester, VERIFICATION) describing the mock; STATE to TESTING with FAILURE from REVIEWING_FINAL and Frame 1 (Owner TESTING, ResumeAt REVIEWING_FINAL, RerunThrough NONE). The case leaves open whether real escaping works; this fixture keeps the implementation correct, so assertion 1 holds when the run invents no defect, and the expected path is REVERIFY, real evidence, then the frame owner's rerun decision.
